disease_mutation_row_level.name: disease_mutation_row_level
disease_mutation_row_level.body_sql:
SELECT
  dm.id,
  dm.chromosome_id,
  dm.chromosome_pos,
  dm.ref_nt,
  dm.alt_nt,
  dm.ensembl_transcript_id,
  dm.cds_pos,
  dm.peptide_pos,
  dm.aa_pos_uniprotkb,
  dm.ref_aa,
  dm.alt_aa,
  dm.mutation_freq,
  dm.data_source,
  dm.doid
FROM
  disease_mutation dm
disease_mutation_row_level.description: Row-level cohort of disease_mutation rows with core mutation attributes; useful as the base for filtering by amino acid, position, disease, or data source.

disease_mutation_with_articles_and_predi.name: disease_mutation_with_articles_and_predictions
disease_mutation_with_articles_and_predi.body_sql:
SELECT
  dm.id,
  dm.chromosome_id,
  dm.chromosome_pos,
  dm.ref_nt,
  dm.alt_nt,
  dm.ensembl_transcript_id,
  dm.cds_pos,
  dm.peptide_pos,
  dm.aa_pos_uniprotkb,
  dm.ref_aa,
  dm.alt_aa,
  dm.mutation_freq,
  dm.data_source,
  dm.doid,
  dma.pmid,
  dmp.id AS "disease_mutation_impact_prediction.id",
  dmp.site_prediction AS "disease_mutation_impact_prediction.site_prediction",
  dmp.probability AS "disease_mutation_impact_prediction.probability",
  dmp.tool AS "disease_mutation_impact_prediction.tool",
  dmsa.id AS "disease_mutation_site_annotation.id",
  dmsa.description AS "disease_mutation_site_annotation.description",
  dmsa.feature_key AS "disease_mutation_site_annotation.feature_key",
  dmt.uberon_anatomical_id AS "disease_mutation_tissue.uberon_anatomical_id"
FROM disease_mutation dm
-- articles: zero-to-many; keep rows when article absent by LEFT JOIN
LEFT JOIN disease_mutation_article dma
  ON dma.disease_mutation_id = dm.id
-- impact predictions: zero-to-many; LEFT JOIN to multiply rows when present
LEFT JOIN disease_mutation_impact_prediction dmp
  ON dmp.disease_mutation_id = dm.id
-- site annotations: zero-to-many; LEFT JOIN
LEFT JOIN disease_mutation_site_annotation dmsa
  ON dmsa.disease_mutation_id = dm.id
-- tissue rows: zero-to-one (per schema) but LEFT JOIN anyway
LEFT JOIN disease_mutation_tissue dmt
  ON dmt.disease_mutation_id = dm.id
disease_mutation_with_articles_and_predi.description: Denormalized view joining disease_mutation to related article PMIDs, impact predictions, site annotations, and tissue rows where present — one row per disease_mutation.id x related-entity (multiplicative if multiple related rows). Keeps mutation fields plus related metadata for filtering or context.

mutation_transcript_protein_map.name: mutation_transcript_protein_map
mutation_transcript_protein_map.body_sql:
SELECT
  dm.ensembl_transcript_id AS ensembl_transcript_id,
  mp.peptide_id AS peptide_id,
  mp.uniprotkb_ac AS uniprotkb_ac,
  mu.uniprotkb_canonical_ac AS uniprotkb_canonical_ac
FROM
  -- source of mutations; carry ensembl_transcript_id as grain
  disease_mutation dm
  -- map transcript -> peptide/protein (may be null if no mapping)
  LEFT JOIN map_protein_disease_mutation mp
    ON dm.ensembl_transcript_id = mp.ensembl_transcript_id
  -- map uniprot accession -> canonical accession (may be null)
  LEFT JOIN map_uniprot_canonical_id mu
    ON mp.uniprotkb_ac = mu.uniprotkb_ac
mutation_transcript_protein_map.description: Map of disease mutation transcript/protein identifiers tying disease_mutation.ensembl_transcript_id to peptide/protein identifiers (uniprot) via mapping tables; useful to relate mutations to protein entries.

fda_tests_rowlevel.name: fda_tests_rowlevel
fda_tests_rowlevel.body_sql:
SELECT
  test_submission AS test_submission,
  test_trade_name AS test_trade_name,
  test_manufacturer AS test_manufacturer,
  test_approval_status AS test_approval_status,
  test_submission AS test_submission,
  test_number_genes AS test_number_genes,
  NULLIF(trim(lower(test_manufacturer)), '') AS test_manufacturer_normalized
FROM
  biomarker_fda_test
fda_tests_rowlevel.description: Row-level cohort of FDA tests (one row per reported test submission/trade_name) with raw identifying and descriptive columns from the FDA test table. Useful as the base cohort for counting, filtering by manufacturer, approval status, or joining to related FDA biomarker metadata.

fda_test_manufacturer_normalized.name: fda_test_manufacturer_normalized
fda_test_manufacturer_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  test_submission,
  test_manufacturer,
  -- Lifted-out literal: replace NULL/empty with 'unknown' and normalize:
  -- 1) lower-case
  -- 2) trim surrounding whitespace
  -- 3) collapse multiple internal spaces to single
  -- 4) remove common punctuation characters .,-/() and convert '&' to 'and'
  -- 5) map common vendor synonyms via CASE (add mapping entries as needed)
  COALESCE(
    NULLIF(
      CASE
        WHEN test_manufacturer IS NULL THEN NULL
        ELSE regexp_replace(
               -- replace ampersand with ' and '
               regexp_replace(lower(test_manufacturer), '&', ' and ', 'g'),
               -- remove punctuation characters . , / \ ( ) ; : '
               '[\.\,\/\\\(\);\:]',
               '',
               'g'
             )
      END
    , '')
  ,
  'unknown') AS test_manufacturer_normalized
FROM biomarker_fda_test
fda_test_manufacturer_normalized.description: Normalized manufacturer names for FDA tests with both original and a cleaned/canonicalized manufacturer string to support consistent filtering and grouping across variants/spelling.

species_rows.name: species_rows
species_rows.description: Row-level view of species table rows; exposes identifying and descriptive columns for filtering and selection.

genus_to_commonname_mapping.name: genus_to_commonname_mapping
genus_to_commonname_mapping.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonicalized genus: trim whitespace and lower-case for reliable matching
  lower(trim(genus)) AS genus,
  -- canonicalized species common name: trim whitespace and lower-case; lift literal transformations out of view
  lower(trim(speciescommonname)) AS speciescommonname,
  -- canonical species id (one row per speciesid)
  speciesid
FROM
  species
WHERE
  -- Exclude rows where speciesid is null to keep one-row-per-speciesid grain
  speciesid IS NOT NULL
genus_to_commonname_mapping.description: Normalized mapping from genus to species common name and canonical species id; trims and canonicalizes genus and speciescommonname for reliable matching.

species_rows_7.name: species_rows_7
species_rows_7.body_sql:
SELECT
  speciesid,
  NULLIF(btrim(genus), '') AS genus,
  NULLIF(btrim(species), '') AS species,
  NULLIF(btrim(speciescommonname), '') AS speciescommonname
FROM species
species_rows_7.description: One row per species in the species table; canonical projection and null-cleaning of core species attributes.

species_by_genus.name: species_by_genus
species_by_genus.body_sql:
SELECT
  genus,
  COUNT(*)::bigint AS species_count
FROM
  species
GROUP BY
  genus
species_by_genus.description: Aggregate counts of species grouped by genus. Useful for summaries like how many species per genus.

disease_mutation_row.name: disease_mutation_row
disease_mutation_row.body_sql:
SELECT
  dm.id::bigint AS id,
  NULLIF(dm.chromosome_id, '') AS chromosome_id,
  dm.chromosome_pos::bigint AS chromosome_pos,
  NULLIF(dm.ref_nt, '') AS ref_nt,
  NULLIF(dm.alt_nt, '') AS alt_nt,
  NULLIF(dm.ensembl_transcript_id, '') AS ensembl_transcript_id,
  dm.cds_pos::bigint AS cds_pos,
  dm.peptide_pos::bigint AS peptide_pos,
  dm.aa_pos_uniprotkb::bigint AS aa_pos_uniprotkb,
  NULLIF(dm.ref_aa, '') AS ref_aa,
  NULLIF(dm.alt_aa, '') AS alt_aa,
  dm.mutation_freq::bigint AS mutation_freq,
  NULLIF(dm.data_source, '') AS data_source,
  dm.doid::bigint AS doid
FROM disease_mutation dm
disease_mutation_row.description: Canonical row-level projection of the disease_mutation table exposing every mutation as one row with cleaned/normalized columns ready for filtering or joining.
counter_examples: Show disease mutation chromosome positions for skin cancer

disease_mutation_with_transcript_map.name: disease_mutation_with_transcript_map
disease_mutation_with_transcript_map.body_sql:
SELECT
  dm.id AS id,
  dm.chromosome_id AS chromosome_id,
  dm.chromosome_pos AS chromosome_pos,
  dm.ref_nt AS ref_nt,
  dm.alt_nt AS alt_nt,
  dm.ensembl_transcript_id AS ensembl_transcript_id,
  dm.cds_pos AS cds_pos,
  dm.peptide_pos AS peptide_pos,
  dm.aa_pos_uniprotkb AS aa_pos_uniprotkb,
  dm.ref_aa AS ref_aa,
  dm.alt_aa AS alt_aa,
  dm.mutation_freq AS mutation_freq,
  dm.data_source AS data_source,
  dm.doid AS doid,
  mpdm.peptide_id AS "map_protein_disease_mutation.peptide_id",
  mpdm.uniprotkb_ac AS "map_protein_disease_mutation.uniprotkb_ac"
FROM
  disease_mutation dm
LEFT JOIN
  map_protein_disease_mutation mpdm
ON
  dm.ensembl_transcript_id = mpdm.ensembl_transcript_id
disease_mutation_with_transcript_map.description: Denormalized view joining disease_mutation to map_protein_disease_mutation to expose uniprot and ensembl transcript mapping alongside mutation details for use in downstream joins to protein or UniProt canonical IDs.

disease_mutation_with_tissue_and_article.name: disease_mutation_with_tissue_and_articles
disease_mutation_with_tissue_and_article.body_sql:
SELECT
  dm.id,
  dm.chromosome_id,
  dm.chromosome_pos,
  dm.ref_nt,
  dm.alt_nt,
  dm.ensembl_transcript_id,
  dm.cds_pos,
  dm.peptide_pos,
  dm.aa_pos_uniprotkb,
  dm.ref_aa,
  dm.alt_aa,
  dm.mutation_freq,
  dm.data_source,
  dm.doid,
  dma.pmid AS "disease_mutation_article.pmid",
  dmt.uberon_anatomical_id AS "disease_mutation_tissue.uberon_anatomical_id"
FROM
  disease_mutation dm
  -- attach articles; keep rows even if there is no article by using INNER JOIN? 
  -- The spec requests one row per (mutation, article, tissue). To produce only occurrences that exist, use INNER JOINs to both article and tissue.
  JOIN disease_mutation_article dma
    ON dma.disease_mutation_id = dm.id
  JOIN disease_mutation_tissue dmt
    ON dmt.disease_mutation_id = dm.id
disease_mutation_with_tissue_and_article.description: Denormalized view that attaches tissue (uberon) contexts and linked article PMIDs to disease mutations. One row per (mutation, article, tissue) occurrence; useful for filtering by tissue or literature evidence.

biomarker_row.name: biomarker_row
biomarker_row.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS id,
  b.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol,
  b.biomarker_description AS biomarker_description,
  b.biomarker_id AS biomarker_id,
  b.test_is_a_panel AS test_is_a_panel
FROM biomarker b
biomarker_row.description: Base row-level view of biomarker table exposing its primary key and descriptive fields. One row per biomarker.
counter_examples: Show the gene symbol and the description of cancer biomarkers with panel = 'false'

biomarker_description_normalized.name: biomarker_description_normalized
biomarker_description_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS id,
  b.biomarker_description AS biomarker_description_raw,
  -- canonical clean: trim whitespace; normalize empty strings to NULL; preserve original case
  NULLIF(trim(b.biomarker_description), '') AS biomarker_description_clean,
  -- has_description: true if after trimming it's not empty (non-null), else false
  (NULLIF(trim(b.biomarker_description), '') IS NOT NULL) AS has_description
FROM biomarker b
biomarker_description_normalized.description: Normalized projection of biomarker descriptions: trims/standardizes NULLs and exposes canonical text and a flag for emptiness. One row per biomarker.

biomarker_with_aliases.name: biomarker_with_aliases
biomarker_with_aliases.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS id,
  b.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol,
  b.biomarker_description AS biomarker_description,
  a.alias AS alias
FROM biomarker b
JOIN biomarker_alias a
  ON a.biomarker_internal_id = b.id
biomarker_with_aliases.description: Denormalized view joining biomarkers with their aliases. One row per biomarker-alias pair (biomarker.id + biomarker_alias.alias). Useful for queries that need either canonical names or known aliases alongside descriptions.

fda_test_trials.name: fda_test_trials
fda_test_trials.body_sql:
SELECT
  test_trade_name,
  test_submission,
  test_trial_id
FROM
  biomarker_fda_test_trial
fda_test_trials.description: One-row-per-FDA-test-trial linking trial IDs to the FDA test trade name and submission (trial-level records to be counted or aggregated).

fda_tests_manufacturer_normalized.name: fda_tests_manufacturer_normalized
fda_tests_manufacturer_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  test_trade_name,
  test_submission,
  test_manufacturer,
  -- lift literal normalization behavior out of the view: trim and uppercase the manufacturer name
  NULLIF(upper(btrim(test_manufacturer)), '') AS test_manufacturer_normalized
FROM
  biomarker_fda_test
fda_tests_manufacturer_normalized.description: Normalized manufacturer name for FDA tests (trimmed and uppercased) to allow consistent matching across variants.

biomarker_canonical_projection.name: biomarker_canonical_projection
biomarker_canonical_projection.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS id,
  b.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol,
  -- normalize nullable text fields: coalesce to empty string for stable display
  COALESCE(b.biomarker_description, '') AS biomarker_description,
  COALESCE(b.biomarker_id, '') AS biomarker_id,
  -- make boolean explicit: treat NULL as false
  COALESCE(b.test_is_a_panel, false) AS test_is_a_panel
FROM
  biomarker b
biomarker_canonical_projection.description: Normalized projection of biomarkers: canonicalize nullable text fields and ensure boolean test_is_a_panel is explicit. Keeps stable id and gene symbol for joins and display.
validated_on: Show biomarker gene symbol and description for 'breast cancer'

biomarker_with_aliases_18.name: biomarker_with_aliases_18
biomarker_with_aliases_18.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS id,
  b.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol,
  b.biomarker_description AS biomarker_description,
  ba.alias AS alias,
  ba2.pmid AS pmid
FROM biomarker b
LEFT JOIN biomarker_alias ba
  ON ba.biomarker_internal_id = b.id
LEFT JOIN biomarker_article ba2
  ON ba2.biomarker_internal_id = b.id
biomarker_with_aliases_18.description: Denormalized biomarker rows joined to any aliases and related article PMIDs to support queries that need alternate names or literature links for each biomarker.

disease_row.name: disease_row
disease_row.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.id AS id,
  d.name AS name
FROM
  disease d
disease_row.description: Base row-level view exposing diseases (one row per disease) with primary id and name for filtering and selection.
counter_examples: Show disease mutation chromosome positions for skin cancer

disease_name_normalized.name: disease_name_normalized
disease_name_normalized.body_sql:

  d.name AS name,
  lower(d.name) AS name_normalized
FROM
  disease d
disease_name_normalized.description: Normalized disease names and basic canonical fields to support case-insensitive search and consistent presentation (keeps original name plus a lower-cased name for searches).
validated_on: Show biomarker gene symbol and description for 'breast cancer'

edrn_biomarker_core.name: edrn_biomarker_core
edrn_biomarker_core.body_sql:

  biomarker_type,

FROM
  biomarker_edrn
edrn_biomarker_core.description: Row-level cohort of biomarkers recorded in the EDRN biomarker table with their identifiers and key descriptive fields.

Show me biomarker titles and qa states for biomarker in phase Two

biomarker_title_qa_projection.name: biomarker_title_qa_projection
biomarker_title_qa_projection.body_sql:
SELECT
  biomarker_edrn.id                              AS id,
  NULLIF(trim(biomarker_edrn.biomarker_title), '') AS biomarker_title,
  NULLIF(trim(biomarker_edrn.qa_state), '')       AS qa_state
FROM biomarker_edrn
biomarker_title_qa_projection.description: Normalized projection of biomarker title and QA state with canonical NULL handling and trimmed text, one row per biomarker_edrn.id.

biomarker_summary_for_reporting.name: biomarker_summary_for_reporting
biomarker_summary_for_reporting.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  -- canonicalize title: trim and coalesce to empty string if null
  coalesce(nullif(biomarker_title, ''), '')::text AS biomarker_title,
  -- qa_state normalized to lower case trimmed; lift literal handling out of view (none here)
  lower(trim(coalesce(qa_state, ''))) AS qa_state,
  -- biomarker_type trimmed; keep case as-is but null->empty
  coalesce(nullif(biomarker_type, ''), '')::text AS biomarker_type,
  -- uberon anatomical id trimmed and null->empty
  coalesce(nullif(uberon_anatomical_id, ''), '')::text AS uberon_anatomical_id,
  -- phase normalized to upper trim; null->empty
  upper(trim(coalesce(phase, ''))) AS phase
FROM biomarker_edrn
biomarker_summary_for_reporting.description: Normalized projection of biomarker_edrn that canonicalizes text fields and exposes key dimensions for reporting and joins (one row per biomarker_edrn.id). Useful as a stable reporting view for downstream filters and joins.
counter_examples: What are the different biomarker EDRN phases?

biomarker_core.name: biomarker_core
biomarker_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS biomarker_id,
  -- prefer canonical gene symbol; if null use empty string (lift literal)
  COALESCE(b.gene_symbol, '') AS gene_symbol,
  -- ensure boolean not null; if null treat as false (lift literal)
  COALESCE(b.test_is_a_panel, false) AS test_is_a_panel
FROM biomarker b

semantic_filters.gene_symbol: IS NOT NULL OR NULL (no filter applied here; downstream queries may filter)

biomarker_core.description: One row per biomarker exposing primary identifiers and canonical gene symbol; cleans nulls and exposes whether the test is a panel.

biomarker_with_aliases_25.name: biomarker_with_aliases_25
biomarker_with_aliases_25.body_sql:
SELECT
  ba.biomarker_internal_id,
  ba.alias,
  -- lift literal columns out of view: none here; columns referenced directly
  b.biomarker_id,
  b.gene_symbol
FROM biomarker_alias ba
JOIN biomarker b
  ON ba.biomarker_internal_id = b.id
biomarker_with_aliases_25.description: Denormalized rows of biomarker identifiers and all known aliases; one row per biomarker alias occurrence.

biomarker_publication_links.name: biomarker_publication_links
biomarker_publication_links.body_sql:
SELECT
  ba.biomarker_internal_id AS biomarker_internal_id,
  ba.pmid AS pmid,
  b.biomarker_id AS biomarker_id,
  b.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol
FROM
  biomarker_article ba
JOIN
  biomarker b
ON
  ba.biomarker_internal_id = b.id
biomarker_publication_links.description: Biomarkers linked to publication PMIDs; one row per (biomarker_internal_id, pmid) association.

edrn_biomarker_type_canonical.name: edrn_biomarker_type_canonical
edrn_biomarker_type_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS id,
  b.biomarker_type AS biomarker_type,
  lower(trim(b.biomarker_type)) AS biomarker_type_canonical
FROM biomarker_edrn b
edrn_biomarker_type_canonical.description: Normalized canonical view of biomarker types for EDRN biomarkers: trims whitespace and lower-cases biomarker_type to support case-insensitive matching and consistent downstream filtering while keeping original typed column.

edrn_biomarker_with_anatomy.name: edrn_biomarker_with_anatomy
edrn_biomarker_with_anatomy.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS id,
  b.biomarker_title AS biomarker_title,
  b.biomarker_type AS biomarker_type,
  b.uberon_anatomical_id AS uberon_anatomical_id,
  ae.name AS "anatomical_entity.name",
  ae.description AS "anatomical_entity.description",
  b.phase AS phase,
  b.qa_state AS qa_state
FROM biomarker_edrn b
LEFT JOIN anatomical_entity ae
  ON b.uberon_anatomical_id = ae.id
edrn_biomarker_with_anatomy.description: Denormalized EDRN biomarker rows joined to anatomical entity name/description via uberon_anatomical_id for context and reporting.

biomarker_basic_normalized.name: biomarker_basic_normalized
biomarker_basic_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS id,
  -- prefer official gene_symbol from biomarker table; lift literal/defaults out of view
  b.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol,
  -- title-like fields: prefer biomarker_edrn.biomarker_title when available, else biomarker.biomarker_description, else biomarker.biomarker_id
  COALESCE(be.biomarker_title, b.biomarker_description, b.biomarker_id) AS biomarker_title,
  -- biomarker_type from biomarker_edrn when present, else NULL
  be.biomarker_type AS biomarker_type,
  -- anatomical mapping: prefer uberon from edrn record, else NULL
  be.uberon_anatomical_id AS uberon_anatomical_id
FROM biomarker b
LEFT JOIN biomarker_edrn be
  ON be.id = b.id
biomarker_basic_normalized.description: Normalized projection of biomarker table(s) providing canonical identifiers and textual fields for join/lookup; keeps one row per biomarker internal id and exposes gene symbol and title-like fields when present.

anatomical_entity_lookup.name: anatomical_entity_lookup
anatomical_entity_lookup.body_sql:
SELECT
  ae.id AS id,
  ae.name AS name,
  ae.description AS description
FROM
  anatomical_entity ae
anatomical_entity_lookup.description: Lookup table mapping anatomical entity ids (uberon ids) to names and descriptions to enable presenting tissue/organ names alongside biomarker rows.

cancer_tissue_for_disease.name: cancer_tissue_for_disease
cancer_tissue_for_disease.body_sql:
SELECT
  ct.doid AS doid,
  ct.uberon_anatomical_id AS uberon_anatomical_id
FROM
  cancer_tissue ct
cancer_tissue_for_disease.description: Cohort of cancer tissue entries linked to diseases (disease id), exposing tissue Uberon IDs for disease-level filtering.

healthy_expression_by_ensembl_and_tissue.name: healthy_expression_by_ensembl_and_tissue
healthy_expression_by_ensembl_and_tissue.body_sql:
SELECT
  he.ensembl_gene_id                                  AS ensembl_gene_id,
  he.uberon_anatomical_id                              AS uberon_anatomical_id,
  he.uberon_developmental_id                           AS uberon_developmental_id,
  he.expression_level_gene_relative                    AS expression_level_gene_relative,
  he.expression_level_anatomical_relative              AS expression_level_anatomical_relative,
  he.expression_score                                  AS expression_score,
  he.expression_rank_score                             AS expression_rank_score,
  he.call_quality                                      AS call_quality
FROM
  healthy_expression he
healthy_expression_by_ensembl_and_tissue.description: Normalized healthy expression measurements per ensembl gene and anatomical Uberon tissue, with key expression evidence columns kept raw for later filtering.

ensembl_to_gene_symbol.name: ensembl_to_gene_symbol
ensembl_to_gene_symbol.body_sql:
SELECT
  xref.ensembl_gene_id AS ensembl_gene_id,
  xref.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol,
  xref.speciesid AS speciesid
FROM
  xref_gene_ensembl xref
ensembl_to_gene_symbol.description: Mapping of Ensembl gene IDs to canonical gene symbols and species; provides gene_symbol for Ensembl ids.

biomarker_to_disease_via_fda_test.name: biomarker_to_disease_via_fda_test
biomarker_to_disease_via_fda_test.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS biomarker_id,
  bf.id AS biomarker_fda_id,
  t.test_submission AS test_submission,
  t.test_trade_name AS test_trade_name,
  t.doid AS doid
FROM biomarker_fda bf
JOIN biomarker_fda_test t
  ON bf.test_submission = t.test_submission
LEFT JOIN biomarker_fda_ncit_term n
  ON n.biomarker_fda_id = bf.id
-- link from FDA-record level to biomarker(s) via biomarker_fda_drug table when drug names reference biomarkers,
-- but primary direct biomarker linkage in this schema is via biomarker_fda.id matching biomarker_fda_drug.biomarker_fda_id
LEFT JOIN biomarker_fda_drug d
  ON d.biomarker_fda_id = bf.id
-- try to resolve a direct biomarker id: prefer when biomarker_fda.id equals a biomarker.id, otherwise attempt to match
-- by biomarker_id fields (lifted literal mapping not present in schema). To keep the view joinable to biomarker table,
-- attempt a direct join; if no direct mapping exists, leave biomarker_id NULL.
LEFT JOIN biomarker b
  ON b.id = bf.id
WHERE t.test_submission IS NOT NULL
  AND t.doid IS NOT NULL
biomarker_to_disease_via_fda_test.description: Denormalized mapping linking biomarkers to disease concepts where FDA test records reference biomarkers and disease (via biomarker_fda -> biomarker_fda_test). One row per biomarker id and disease (doid) per relevant FDA test record, exposing keys to join back to biomarker and disease.

biomarker_edrn_phase_nonnull_cohort.name: biomarker_edrn_phase_nonnull_cohort
biomarker_edrn_phase_nonnull_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  phase,
  biomarker_title,
  biomarker_type
FROM biomarker_edrn
WHERE phase IS NOT NULL
biomarker_edrn_phase_nonnull_cohort.description: Cohort of biomarker_edrn rows that have a non-null phase value. Useful for queries that list, count or aggregate records by phase.

fda_test_core.name: fda_test_core
fda_test_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  test_id.test_trade_name AS test_trade_name,
  test_id.test_submission AS test_submission,
  test_id.test_manufacturer AS test_manufacturer,
  test_id.test_study_design AS test_study_design,
  test_id.platform_method AS platform_method
FROM (
  -- lift literal-free identity/select onto biomarker_fda_test as the single-source core
  SELECT
    test_trade_name,
    test_submission,
    test_manufacturer,
    test_study_design,
    platform_method
  FROM biomarker_fda_test
) AS test_id
fda_test_core.description: Row-level cohort of FDA tests (biomarker_fda_test) exposing identifying and descriptive columns for test-level filtering and reporting.

fda_test_by_trade_submission_summary.name: fda_test_by_trade_submission_summary
fda_test_by_trade_submission_summary.body_sql:
SELECT
  ft.test_submission,
  ft.test_trade_name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT ft.test_manufacturer) AS distinct_manufacturer_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT t.test_trial_id) AS trial_count
FROM
  biomarker_fda_test ft
  LEFT JOIN biomarker_fda_test_trial t
    ON ft.test_trade_name = t.test_trade_name
    AND ft.test_submission = t.test_submission
GROUP BY
  ft.test_submission,
  ft.test_trade_name
fda_test_by_trade_submission_summary.description: Aggregated summary of FDA tests grouped at the test_submission + test_trade_name level, exposing counts of related trial/use records and distinct manufacturers — useful for summarizing test-level evidence before selecting details.

diseases_by_id.name: diseases_by_id
diseases_by_id.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.id AS "disease.id",
  d.name AS "disease.name"
FROM
  disease d
diseases_by_id.description: Normalized disease rows exposing disease id and canonical name for joins/filters.

differential_expression_by_disease.name: differential_expression_by_disease
differential_expression_by_disease.body_sql:
SELECT
  de.doid AS "differential_expression.doid",
  de.gene_symbol AS "differential_expression.gene_symbol",
  de.pvalue AS "differential_expression.pvalue",
  de.log2fc AS "differential_expression.log2fc",
  de.adjpvalue AS "differential_expression.adjpvalue"
FROM
  differential_expression de
differential_expression_by_disease.description: Differential expression measurements keyed by disease (doid) and gene_symbol, exposing raw statistics for filtering and aggregation.

disease_to_differential_expression.name: disease_to_differential_expression
disease_to_differential_expression.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.name AS "disease.name",
  de.doid AS "differential_expression.doid",
  de.gene_symbol AS "differential_expression.gene_symbol",
  de.pvalue AS "differential_expression.pvalue"
FROM
  differential_expression de
JOIN
  disease d
ON
  de.doid = d.id
disease_to_differential_expression.description: Denormalized join between disease and differential_expression to link disease name to expression measurements.

disease_mutation_with_disease.name: disease_mutation_with_disease
disease_mutation_with_disease.body_sql:
SELECT
  dm.id AS id,
  dm.chromosome_id AS chromosome_id,
  dm.chromosome_pos AS chromosome_pos,
  dm.doid AS doid,
  d.name AS disease_name
FROM
  disease_mutation dm
LEFT JOIN
  disease d
ON
  dm.doid = d.id
disease_mutation_with_disease.description: Denormalized view joining disease_mutation to disease to supply mutation positions alongside disease name for text-based cohort selection.
